nota: F120–F124. PENDENTE (Sala, item 7) → achado palavra por palavra: 'The Treaty dams and reservoirs inundated 110,000 hectares (270,000 acres) of Canadian ecosystems, displaced more than two thousand residents as well as First Nations, communities and infrastructure' (governo da BC, 'About the Columbia River Treaty'). Se for à tela, imperial primeiro: '270,000 ACRES (110,000 HA)'. O 'more than two thousand' da mesma página confere com o 'Approximately 2,300' de 2012. Quem libera é o verificador, com o redator.
conversoes: 110,000 ha ÷ 0.40469 = 271,816 acres (a fonte arredonda para 270,000) = 425 sq mi

≈ 2,300 PEOPLE DISPLACED · MORE THAN 12 COMMUNITIES FLOODED
texto_aprovado: Before the treaty dams, people lived along these valleys. The government of British Columbia puts the count at about 2,300 people displaced, and more than a dozen small communities flooded. Some, like Edgewood and Burton, were relocated. Renata no longer exists. Farther north, the river's big bend in British Columbia went under another of the treaty's lakes, and a town went under with it.
